kicker: Pharma CDMOs · Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin and sales
title: CDMOs with orders back added up to 10 pts of margin
dek: Divi's, Laurus, Anthem and Piramal Pharma widened Q2 FY27 EBITDA margins by 5.5–9.9 pts as orders returned. Syngene, Neuland and Cohance, whose sales fell 9–14%, gave up 4–14 pts.

chart.title: Change in EBITDA margin, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26
chart.sub: percentage points, filed consolidated results · line = revenue growth YoY

stats.label: Laurus's small-molecule CDMO sales
stats.note: ₹875 cr in Q2 FY27; group EBITDA margin above its 30%+ guide.

stats.label: Divi's Q2 EBITDA margin
stats.note: Above its 32–35% range, which it left unchanged; material cost fell to ~32% of sales from 40% in H1.

stats.label: Cohance's pharma CDMO sales
stats.note: Q2 FY27 YoY; Specialty Chemicals now guided to fall in FY27.

read: The order recovery has reached commercial-scale makers first; research-led and few-molecule books still need H2 to show it.
sources: Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage analysis
notes: EBITDA margins and revenue growth are from consolidated Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE, with EBITDA excluding other income, so they differ from figures quoted on calls: Anthem cited 50.6% including other income, Neuland 22.9% on total income, and Cohance about 10% on an adjusted basis. Laurus and Piramal Pharma run large generics or other businesses beside contract manufacturing, so their margins are company-wide. Syngene's Q2 call was not on the desk; on its Q1 call it guided FY27 revenue to a single-digit decline at a mid-20s margin. Sai Life is shown on filed numbers only. The 'orders back' reading rests on the companies' own commentary on restocking and project timing.
